cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: What's this medicine for?

cues.speaker: Metal Gear
cues.en: I'll analyze it.

cues.speaker: Metal Gear
cues.en: Antacids, a mucosal protectant, H2 blockers.

cues.speaker: Metal Gear
cues.en: Medicine for stomach trouble.

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: Gibson had stomach trouble, yet ate whale meat. Something's wrong.

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: There must have been a reason he had to eat it.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: I'm sorry. I'm Gibson's daughter, Catherine.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: What's wrong, Gillian?

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: I'm sorry, Catherine. Your father's death was my fault.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Gillian!

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: No. If I'd reached the scene a little sooner, your father...

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: No, I... I knew this could happen to my father.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Every day I saw him off, I knew this day might come.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Would it be today? Tomorrow? His work was dangerous.

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: Catherine, are you...?

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: I am a JUNKER's daughter, after all. So...

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: Will you be all right on your own?

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Don't worry. I can manage on my own.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Besides, I'm too tired to cry anymore.

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: Ah... Catherine...

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Come on, Mr. JUNKER. You have work to do.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Keeping busy helps take my mind off it. So...

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: All right, Catherine. Then I'll need your help.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Alice is barking. Is something out there?

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: A Snatcher?

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: Wait here, Catherine!

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Observations on Snatchers.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Why do Snatchers appear in winter? Why are they nocturnal?

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: I have found the answers to these questions.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: The Snatchers' vampire-like habits all serve one purpose:

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: avoiding sunlight.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: They avoid sunlight because their artificial skin is imperfect.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Prolonged exposure to ultraviolet light causes abnormal growth

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: of melanocytes in the skin's basal layer,

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: producing a skin cancer resembling malignant melanoma.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: What humans call sunburn can be fatal to them.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: This link between ultraviolet light and artificial

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: skin should be the key to tracking down the Snatchers.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Their artificial skin takes at least six months to fully settle.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: These findings suggest several ways to identify a Snatcher.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: 1. Examine the skin. Check for signs of malignant melanoma.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: 2. Check for an odor.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: If the skin is cancerous,

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: the cancer cells emit a distinctive foul smell.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: 3. Check for pollen.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Snatchers seem to be hiding in an area

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: where a special cedar called Snow Cedar grows.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Its pollen is always found wherever they appear.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Snow Cedar is an allergen that causes sore throats,

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: sneezing and more.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: 4. Check for sunscreen.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Snatchers wear sunscreen even in midwinter

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: to protect their skin from ultraviolet light.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Sunscreen blocks medium-wave UV, which causes sunburn,

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: and long-wave UV, which causes tanning.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Of these clues, 1 and 4 should be especially useful.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: They must also repair cancerous artificial skin,

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: not just prevent it.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: At last, I have found their hospital.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: P.S.

cues.speaker: Gibson
cues.en: Beware of a bounty hunter named Randam Hajile.

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: Oh, it's just a crow.

cues.speaker: Metal Gear
cues.en: What a needless scare!

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: So that's what you're like? Get out! Don't come back!

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: I'll give you my address and videophone number, just in case.

cues.speaker: Gillian
cues.en: Call me if anything happens.

cues.speaker: Catherine
cues.en: Thank you. Goodbye.
